content.title: How to watch Houston Astros vs. Los Angeles Angels for free on Apple TV Plus today
content.text: If you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation.HOUSTON – The Los Angeles Angels and Houston Astros meet under the national spotlight tonight – Friday, March 27 – as the second game of the season is featured on Apple TV+ as part of an exclusive weekly doubleheader on “Friday Night Baseball.”The matchup presents an early test for two AL West clubs navigating roster turnover and new identities. The game will be played at Daikin Park in Houston with the broadcast scheduled for 8:15 p.m. Eastern on Apple TV+.Apple TV Plus offers a 7-day free trial. After the free trial period, you can cancel or stay subscribed to Apple TV+ for $12.99 per month.For the Angels, the 2026 season has begun with significant roster reshuffling and a series of injuries impacting both their pitching staff and infield depth. Despite the turbulence, Los Angeles enters with optimism thanks to several recent additions designed to stabilize their rotation and reinforce their lineup. As the franchise continues transitioning under new leadership after recent coaching changes, Friday’s game provides an opportunity to measure how these moves are coming together.Houston, meanwhile, continues its tradition of calculated roster management — balancing cost‑controlled talent with targeted additions aimed at sustaining contention. With several notable transactions, including arbitration agreements, trades and minor‑league signings, the Astros’ front office once again retooled a roster that remains among the AL West’s most competitive. The club also added pitching depth and outfield help, reinforcing a roster built to withstand long‑season attrition.Angels major offseason movesThe Angels made several noteworthy moves aimed at stabilizing the roster. Key additions include Yusei Kikuchi, signed to a three-year deal to bolster the rotation; power-hitting outfielder Jorge Soler, acquired via trade; veteran catcher Travis d’Arnaud and versatile infielder Kevin Newman.The franchise also enacted major leadership changes, parting ways with manager Ron Washington and GM Ray Montgomery as they attempted to reset the team’s long-term direction. Additional transactions included the signing of lefty reliever Joey Lucchesi, and the selection of infielders Adam Frazier and Jeimer Candelario to the big-league roster, moves intended to strengthen depth while multiple pitchers opened the season on the injured list.Astros major offseason movesHouston’s offseason featured a mix of arbitration settlements, trades and depth signings. Among the highlights: the acquisition of Joey Loperfido from Toronto; multiple one‑year contract agreements with key contributors such as Hunter Brown, Jeremy Peña, Bryan Abreu and Jake Meyers and the addition of pitcher Kai‑Wei Teng in a trade with San Francisco. The Astros also secured outfield reinforcement by adding Jesús Sánchez earlier in the cycle. Collectively, these moves helped maintain a competitive core while reinforcing organizational depth.What happened on Opening Day?Friday night’s game is the second game of this opening series between the Angels and Astros. On Thursday, Los Angeles opened the season with a 3-0 win.Angels star Mike Trout, who has been plagued with injuries throughout his storied career, homered to launch what he hopes will be a bounce-back season, according to the Associated Press. Trout also walked three times and played center field for the first time since April 2024.The pitching matchupFriday’s confirmed pitching matchup will see Yusei Kikuchi take the mound for the Angels against Houston right‑hander Mike Burrows.Kikuchi, the Angels’ prominent offseason rotation upgrade, looks to establish himself early as a frontline presence after arriving on a major contract designed to improve a rotation that has struggled with injuries. His left-handed arsenal and strikeout capabilities will be crucial as he faces a Houston lineup known for plate discipline and situational hitting.For the Astros, Burrows enters the showdown as a developing arm, aiming to seize his opportunity in a reworked Astros rotation.Who is announcing Astros vs. Angels? Friday night’s Apple TV+ broadcast will feature members of the network’s regular “Friday Night Baseball” announcing teams, including Wayne Randazzo (play-by-play), Dontrelle Willis (analyst) and Heidi Watney (reporter).What are the latest odds for Houston Astros vs. Los Angeles Angels?
